continuation_reasoning:
DEMAND DETERMINE PRICE IN A FREE MARKET THROUGH THE INTERACTION OF BUYERS AND SELLERS. WHEN DEMAND INCREASES (MORE PEOPLE WANT TO BUY A GOOD OR SERVICE), AND SUPPLY REMAINS THE SAME, PRICES RISE BECAUSE BUYERS COMPETE FOR LIMITED GOODS. CONVERSELY, IF SUPPLY INCREASES (MORE GOOD AVAILABLE) AND DEMAND IS UNCHANGED, PRICES FALL AS SELLERS COMPETE FOR BUYERS.

THE EQUILIBRIUM PRICE IS WHERE THE QUANTITY DEMANDED EQUALS THE QUANTITY SUPPLIED. THIS IS THE MARKET CLEARING POINT. IF THE PRICE IS ABOVE EQUILIBRIUM, EXCESS SUPPLY OCCURS (SURPLUS), AND SELLERS LOWER PRICES TO SELL THE SURPLUS. IF THE PRICE IS BELOW EQUILIBRIUM, EXCESS DEMAND OCCURS (SHORTAGE), AND BUYERS COMPETE TO BUY LIMITED STOCK, RAISING PRICES.

WHEN A GOVERNMENT IMPOSES A PRICE CEILING (A MAXIMUM PRICE), IT CAN CREATE A SHORTAGE. IF THE CEILING IS BELOW THE EQUILIBRIUM PRICE, SELLERS HAVE LESS INCENTIVE TO SUPPLY THE GOOD OR SERVICE, WHILE DEMAND REMAINS HIGH. THIS LEADS TO SHORTAGES, LONGER WAIT TIMES, LOWER QUALITY, AND BLACK MARKETS MAY EMERGE AS SELLERS TRY TO GET AROUND THE CEILING.

IN SUMMARY, SUPPLY AND DEMAND SET PRICES IN A FREE MARKET, AND PRICE CEILINGS DISTORT THIS MECHANISM, OFTEN LEADING TO SHORTAGES AND REDUCED MARKET EFFICIENCY.

final_answer:
In a free market, prices are determined by the interaction of supply and demand. When demand for a product increases (more people want it) and supply stays the same, buyers compete, pushing prices up. If supply increases (more product available) and demand stays the same, sellers compete, lowering prices. The equilibrium price is where the quantity buyers want equals the quantity sellers offer.

When a government imposes a price ceiling (a maximum price), it can create shortages. If the ceiling is set below the equilibrium price, sellers are less motivated to supply the product, while demand remains high. This results in shortages, longer wait times, reduced quality, and sometimes black markets. The ceiling disrupts the market mechanism, often reducing efficiency and harming both buyers and sellers.
